text:
And what if we keep moving ahead

from smile to smile

until the last hope?


So what?

And what do you give me,

me, who have lost my name,

the name that was sweet substance to me

in remote times, when I was not myself

but a girl deceived by her blood?


Why, why

this undoing of myself, this bleeding out,

this plucking myself, this losing my balance

if my reality retreats

as if driven back by machine-gun fire

and suddenly breaks into a run,

though they catch up with it all the same,

until it falls at my feet like a dead bird?

I would like to speak of life.

For this is life,

this howl, this driving one's nails

into one's chest, this tearing out

one's hair by handfuls, this spitting

into one's own eyes, only to say,

only to see whether one can say:

“Am I, then? Is it true that I am?

Is it not true that I exist

and am not the nightmare of a beast?”


And with muddy hands

we pound on love's doors.

And with conscience covered

in dirty and beautiful veils,

we plead for God.

And with temples cracking

with idiotic pride

we take life by the waist

and give death a sidelong kick.


For this is what we do.

We get ahead from smile to smile

until the last hope.

translation.title: Much Further Beyond
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves Pizarnik’s abrupt repetitions, bodily violence, and question marks as the poem’s central rhythm.
